---
title: "Module 6: Applied ML Research"
---

<!-- This file is the source of a page on the course website. Read it there: https://ai.buas.nl/open-courses/introduction-to-ml/modules/6_applied_ml_research/00_overview.html -->

A model is only useful when others understand what you did, and research often has a better approach than the one you would come up with yourself. In this module you learn to present and write about technical work, to find and read machine-learning research, and to test an idea from a paper yourself.

## What you will be able to do

After this module you can:

- prepare presentations and documents with your own checklists;
- find, read and judge machine-learning papers;
- test an idea from a paper in your own project and report the evidence.

## Self-study

Work through the activities in order:

1. [Communicating Technical Work](1_self_study/01_communicating_technical_work.qmd), about 4 hours: a lecture on presenting and one on writing, and your own checklists for both.
2. [Understanding ML Research](1_self_study/02_understanding_ml_research.qmd), about 2 hours: types of research output, the scientific method, research metrics, and how to find and access papers.
3. [Research to Practice](1_self_study/03_from_research_to_practice.qmd), about 6 hours: read a machine-learning paper and test one of its principles in a project of your own.
4. [Review](1_self_study/04_review.qmd), about 15 minutes: a summary of the module and a short quiz.

## DataLab

After the Self-study, apply what you learned in the DataLab project: [Iteration 6](2_datalab/00_overview.qmd).
